name: Burrower pearl
description: A lumpy, lustrous pearl the size of a hen's egg, with grains of gold and red garnet grown into its nacre. Cut from the gills of a huge burrowing beast.
notes: A lumpy pearl 56 mm long built from three overlapping balls in `pearl`, with an `iridescent` sheen patch and two `crystal-glow-white` glints for lustre, and three tiny gold and garnet specks on its face. The model shows a pearl a hand can close round.

name: Burrower armour plate
description: A domed slab of armour as big as a shield, ridged where it grew and seamed with a faint blue mineral vein. Heavy enough to stop most things that hit it.
notes: An 840 by 620 mm plate 30 mm thick, domed across its width, with three ridges and two pale blue veins. A plate a shield can be cut from needs the area modelled, so the volume follows the shape.

name: Black spider shell plate
description: A curved plate of glossy black shell cut from a giant spider's back, seamed in dull red, with two short spurs on its crest. Light and hard enough to armour with.
notes: A 460 by 360 mm plate 8 mm thick, curved across its width, with three red seams and two spurs. Lacquer black stands in for the shell; a black chitin finish would read better than lacquer.

name: Black spider fang
description: A hooked black fang as long as a hand, still wet with green venom along its groove, with a ragged scrap of gum at the root.
notes: A fang 150 mm long, curved through about 60 degrees, from 26 mm at the root to a point, with a venom groove and a drop at its tip. Onyx stands in for the fang's glossy black; the material is flesh because the root comes with it, shown as the gum lump.

name: Rune-carved branch
description: A straight branch as long as a walking staff, still in its bark, ringed with carved bands that give off a pale blue glow.
notes: A branch 1.3 m long and 52 mm thick with four glowing rune rings and three glyphs on its front. The glow is painted with aquamarine because no emissive finish exists.

name: Vial of glowing dust
description: A corked glass vial two thirds full of fine pale green dust that gives off a soft light of its own.
notes: Loose powder, modelled in the corked vial a player would pick up: 64 mm tall and 26 mm across. The dust sits flush with the glass wall so it shows through the see-through glass in the game; the tile draws the glass opaque.

name: Glowing reading lamp
description: A small brass-footed glass globe with a ball of soft blue light inside, enough to read by. Its domed brass cover hangs open on a hinge at the back.
notes: A lamp 120 mm tall with its cover swung back, 146 mm deep. The covered lamp is its own model, glow_light_covered. The light's beam and fuel are left to the light framework; the glow core is painted with aquamarine because no emissive finish exists.

name: Glowing reading lamp (covered)
description: A small glass reading lamp with its domed brass cover shut, hiding the light inside.
notes: The covered state of glow_light, a distinct look, so it gets its own model with the cover closed over the globe.

name: Violet glow pearl
description: A flawless clear violet sphere with a small pale blue light at its heart. It feels faintly warm in the hand.
notes: A sphere 48 mm across with a smaller glowing core; the shell is see-through in the game, so the core shows, though the tile draws it opaque. A `crystal-glow-blue` glow on the front face and a `crystal-glow-white` glint carry the light and the clear sphere on the tile. The name avoids the mod's word for magic.

name: Twin-lobed gizzard stone
description: A heavy, smooth stone pinched into two unequal lobes, one sandy and one dark, joined by a band of milky quartz. Taken from the gut of a great beast, it makes a fair hammer.
notes: A two-lobed stone 165 mm long, held by its larger lobe. Hammering 1, the level of a hammering stone. The name describes the stone instead of the mod's creature.

name: Bloodsucker's proboscis
description: A long, stiff feeding tube with a fleshy root, banded in pale rings and tapering to a needle point. It could stab, but not well.
notes: A tube 300 mm long, 14 mm across at its root, held by the tube. No melee block is drafted, as a needle this light would only add a weak stab.

name: Stone eggshell shard
description: A curved, speckled fragment of an egg that had a shell of stone, broken to edges sharp enough to cut with in a pinch.
notes: A curved fragment 124 by 92 mm and 6 mm thick. The outline stays convex because the curved-plate strips must be convex; a jagged edge would need a cut.
